Gold(I) Complexation of Phosphanoxy-Substituted
Phosphaalkenesf or Activation-FreeL AuCl Catalysis
Miki Kato, YasuhiroU eta, and Shigekazu Ito*[a]
Abstract: The phosphanoxy-substituted phosphaalkene
bearingt he P=C@O@Ps keleton can be prepared from di-
phosphene Mes*P=PMes* (Mes* = 2,4,6-tBu3C6H2), and their
use for catalysis is of interest. In this paper,c omplexation of
the phosphanoxy-substituted phosphaalkenes with gold are
investigated, and the catalytic activity of the mono-a nd bis(-
chlorogold) complexes are subsequently evaluated. Reaction
of the P=C@O@Pc ompound with (tht)AuCl (tht = tetrahydro-
thiophene) showed dominant coordination on the sp3 phos-
phorus,a nd complete coordination on the sp2 phosphorus
requiredr emovalo ft etrahydrothiophene. Atoms In Mole-
cules (AIM) analysisb ased on the X-ray structure of the mon-
o(chlorogold) complex indicated ap seudo coordinating in-
teraction between the goldc entera nd the P=Cu nit. The
bis(chlorogold) complexes displayed conformationali somer-
ism, and catalyzed the cycloisomerization/alkoxycyclization
of 1,6-enyne and for hydration of terminal alkyne without
activation treatment. Even the mono(chlorogold) complexes
catalyzed the alkoxycyclizationr eactionsw ithouta silver co-
catalyst,i ndicatingt hat the alcohols were effective in activat-
ing the AuCl unit.
Introduction
Phosphaalkenes bearing P=Cd ouble bond(s) have been uti-
lized as strong p-accepting ligandsb ecause of the low-lying
LUMO levels comparable with that of carbon monoxide( CO).
Although the phosphorus–carbon multiple bondsa re normally
too reactive to isolate, the kinetic stabilization methodu sing
sterically encumbered substituents enables the heavieru nsatu-
rated bonds to be protected from reactive species.[1, 2] So far,
many kinds of isolable low-coordinated organophosphorus
compounds have been reported,[3, 4] and severalt ransition-
metal-based Lewis acid catalysts have been developed.[5, 6]
We have utilized kinetically stabilized phosphaalkenes to de-
velop homogeneous gold catalysis.[7] Homogeneous gold catal-
ysis featuring soft p-acidic character has greatly progressed
over the past few decades, and many catalytic molecular trans-
formationsh ave been established.[8, 9] In general, catalytically
active gold complexes bearing ligated phosphines should not
contain chloride,b ecause the Cl@ ion binds with gold strongly
and prevents coordination of the substrates enough to cause
the following moleculart ransformations.[10] However,s everal
phosphaalkene-chlorogold(I) complexes can catalyzem olecular
transformations withouta ctivation using silver co-catalyst-
s.[5a, 7, 11] It is plausible that the strong p-accepting character of
P=Cc an promote the Lewis acid functionality on the gold cen-
ter(s) even in the presence of Cl@ ion. In addition, most of the
phosphaalkene-chlorogold(I) catalysts can be recovered after
the reactions, whichi sp romising to develop sustainable chem-
ical processes.[12]
The first isolable diphosphene Mes*P = PMes* (Mes* = 2,4,6-
tBu3C6H2,s upermesityl) is one of the key compoundsi nvolved
in the recent progress on the chemistry of multiple bonds in-
cluding heavier main group elements.[13] The “true phospho-
benzene” has been utilized as as tartingm aterial fort he syn-
thesiso fl ow-coordinated phosphorus compounds by cleaving
the P = Pd oubleb ond.[3, 4b] Previously, we described am etathe-
sis-type transformation of Mes*P = PMes* by using an organo-
lithiumr eagent and an acyl chloride, affording phosphanoxy-
substituted phosphaalkene 1 via the P@Pb ond cleavage in the
acyl-substituted diphosphanei ntermediates (Scheme1 ).[14] The
presence of both sp2 ands p3 phosphorus atoms in 1 is quite
attractive as one of the non-symmetric P2 ligands ystems.
Whereas attempted synthesis of chelate transition-metal com-
plexesb earing 1 has been unsuccessful until now,u se of 1 for
the chemistryo fg old complexes has been possible.

In this paper,w ed escribe the preparation and catalytic ac-
tivity of chlorogold(I) complexes bearing 1.A lthough the P=C
unit in 1 basically showsi nferiorc oordination ability to AuCl,
the sp2 phosphorus atom is effective to increaset he catalytic
activity of the gold centere ven in the presenceo fc hloride
ions. In the course of structure determination, the bis(chloro-
gold) complexes displayed dynamic conformational changes.
Interestingly,w eak interaction between the P=Cg roup and the
sp3 phosphanoxy-coordinated gold centeri nt he mono(chloro-
gold) complex might be effective to catalyze the cyclization
process under the activation-free conditions accompanying al-
cohols.
Results and Discussion
Preparation and structure of chlorogold complexes bearing
the ligated P=C@O@Ps ystem
According to our previous report,[14] phosphanoxy-substituted
phosphaalkenes 1 were prepared from diphosphene Mes*P =
PMes*,o rganolithium reagents,a nd benzoyl chloride. Reaction
of 1 with 1e quivalent of (tht)AuCl (tht = tetrahydrothiophene)
allowed predominant coordination of the gold on the sp3
phosphorus in the phosphanoxy group, and the corresponding
mono(chlorogold) complexes 2 were isolated in moderate
yields (Scheme 2, Eq (1)). Shortening the reaction time (2 h)
gave almost the same results. On the other hand, reaction of 1
with 2e quivalents of (tht)AuCl was sluggish and gave mixtures
of bis(chlorogold)c omplexes 3 togetherw ith 2.T his result in-
dicatest hat, in contrastt om ostp hosphaalkenes we have in-
vestigateds of ar,[7] the coordination ability of the P=Cu nit in 1
is considerably weak, probably owing to the presence of the
oxo unit, and comparable with that of tetrahydrothiophene. To
avoid cumbersome purification processes in the synthesis of 3,
the volatile materials including tetrahydrothiophene were re-
moved from the reactionm ixture of 1 and 2e quivalents of
(tht)AuCl, and subsequenta ddition of the solvent (dichlorome-
thane) was conducted. This procedure wass uccessful, and
only bis(chlorogold) complexes 3 were isolated in good yields
(Scheme 2, Eq. (2)). It should be mentioned that de-coordina-
tion of AuCl from the sp2 phosphorus generating gold nano-
particles was somewhat problematic in the preparation and
isolation of 3b .

P=Cm oiety directst owardt he gold centerw itht he P···Au dis-
tance of 3.404 /C138 .T he P2@C1 distance is almostt he same as

chelate interaction, which could be relatedt ot he lower coordi-
nation ability of 2 (see above). The Au@Cl distance of 2.296 /C138
is slightly elongatedc ompared with 3 (see below), indicating

ity on the gold center.T he Atoms in Molecule (AIM) study[15, 16]
showed the trajectory from the sp2 phosphorus atom and the
gold center,i ndicatingb oth ap seudo s-donation from the
lone pair and ab ack-donating p-coordination to the P=Cu nit
(Figure 1b ).[9j] Thus, the presence of the P=C@Os keleton in 2a
might increase the Lewis acidity by weakening the Au@Cl inter-
action. The natural bond orbital( NBO) analysisc ould not give
scalablep arameters depicting the small interaction between
the gold center and the sp2-phosphorus atom.

In the NMR analyses of 3b (R = Ph), the broadened 31PN MR
(121 MHz) signals were observed around d = 140 and 180 ppm
at 298 K( Figure 3a ), which is in sharp contrast with 3a (dP =

might correlate with the rapid interconversion between at
least two conformers. Neithers eparation nor sharpening of the
31PN MR signals was observedb etween 183–323K .P reliminary
DFT calculations for 3b as well as the X-ray structure of 3a in-
dicatedt hat the aurophilic interaction[18] might not be advan-
tageous.T herefore, we speculated that the presence of four ar-
omatic rings in 3b might produce the propeller-type confor-
mations (Figure 3b ). In the 1Hv ariable-temperature (VT)-NMR
analyses (400 MHz, [D8]THF), the aromatic protons showedc oa-

porting Information). By using the Gutowsky–Holm’s formu-

Catalytic activity of bis(chlorogold) complexes bearing the
ligated P=C@O@Ps ystem

complexes can catalyze several molecular transformations by
activating the terminal alkyne units without needing as ilver
co-catalyst.[7a–f] Bis(chlorogold) complexes 3 can also be used
for several catalytic reactions without Ag salts. Tables1 and 2

display the resultsf or the hydration of 2-propynyl acetate and

Both 3a and 3b showed comparable catalytic activityw ith the
mononuclearc hlorogold complex bearing Mes*P=CPh2.[7a]
Complexes 3 showed no decomposition in the hydration and
cycloisomerization reactions.
Table 3s ummarizes the alkoxycyclization of 1,6-enyne cata-
lyzed by 3.W hereas 3a showed am oderate catalytic activity,
3b gave the methylenecyclopentene product in an excellent
yield. However,b oth 3a and 3b showedd e-coordination of
AuCl from the P=Cu nit in the catalytic process, and the mono-
nuclear complexes 2 were obtained after the alkoxycyclization
reaction. Although the detailed mechanism has been unclear,
the sensitive P(sp2)@Au bond to alcohol might correlate with
the lower coordination ability of the sp2 phosphorus in 1.A
considerable amount of the de-coordination product 2b was
found after the catalytic reaction using 3b ,w hich correlated
with the instability observed during the preparation process.
The superior catalytic activity of 3b for the alkoxycyclization
prompted us to examine other catalytic reactions including hy-
droalkoxylation. As shown in Table 4, 2,2-diphenylhexa-4,5-
dien-1-ol wasc onverted into the corresponding 2-vinyltetrahy-
drofurani na low yield (entry 1). Use of AgSbF6 as ac o-catalyst
improved the yield up to 91 %( entry 2).
Mono(chlorogold) complexes (2) for activation-free gold
catalysis
In addition to bis(chlorogold) complexes 3,c atalytic reactions
using the mononuclear complexes 2 were also examined. The
hydration and the cycloisomerization reactions did not occur
in the presence of 2.O nt he other hand, alkoxycyclization of
1,6-enyne was catalyzed in the presence of 2 (Table 5). Both 2a
and 2b provided small amounts of the cyclization product
after 24 h( entries 1, 2). Elongation of the reactiont ime was ef-
fective to improve the yield up to 62 %w ith 2a (entry 3) and,
to our delight, 95 %w ith 2b (entry 4). No decomposition of 2
was observed after the catalytic processes. Warming at 40 8C
was effective to acceleratet he reaction( entries 5, 6). The
ethoxydiphenylphosphine-chlorogold(I) complex 4[20] showed
no catalytic activity,i ndicating that the presence of the P=C
unit in 2 is responsible for the gold-catalyzed the alkoxycycliza-
tion under the activation-free conditions (entry 7). The intra-
molecular hydroalkoxylation of allenyl alcoholw as not facilitat-
ed by 2b even in the presence of AgSbF6 (see the Supporting
Information).
As discussed above,t he presence of the P=C-O skeleton in
2a might increase the Lewis acidity by interacting with the
gold center.A lso, possible hydrogen-bond interactions be-
tween the chloride in 2 and methanol might be advantageous
to the activation-free catalytic alkoxycyclization. Althougha de-
tailed analysiss hould be conducted, Figure4 suggestsa plau-
sible interaction that increases the Lewis acid charactero nt he
gold centeri n 2.[21, 22] In the alkoxycyclization reaction with 3,

To explore the effects of alcohol on the catalytic activity of
the mono(chlorogold) complex in more detail,r eaction of 1,6-
enyne in the presence of other alcohols wasi nvestigated.
Whereas tBuOH deactivated the catalytic functionality of 2b ,
use of 2,2,2-trifluoroethan-1-ol (CF3CH2OH) was quite effective
to promote the cycloisomerization process (Scheme 3). Al-
thought he low nucleophilicity of CF3CH2OH wasu seless for
the alkoxylation process, the increased Lewis acid character by
the perfluorinated ethanol wass uitable to activate the alkyne
unit leading to the vinylcyclopentene product.
Conclusion
We described the utility of the phosphaoxy-substituted phos-
phaalkenesf or activation-free gold catalysis. The mononuclear
structureo f 2 displayed weak interaction between the P=C
unit and the gold center,w hich might increase the Lewis acidi-
ty.B is(chlorogold) complexes 3 did not contain the aurophilic
interaction, and showed conformational isomerism probably
owing to the presence of four aryl substituents. Bis(chlorogold)
complexes 3 containing the P(sp2)@Au bond catalyzed cycloiso-
merization/alkoxycyclization of 1,6-enynea nd hydration of 2-
propynyl acetate withouta ny activation treatment. Interesting-
ly,e ven mono(chlorogold) complexes 2 showed catalytic activi-
ty in the alkoxycyclization, indicating the additional effectso f
alcohol for increasing the Lewis acidity.T he findings of this
study suggest an ovel design for sustainable goldc atalysis as
well as for elucidation of catalytic mechanismsp romoted by
the phosphaalkene unit.
Experimental Section
All experiments were carried out under inert atmosphere (nitrogen
or argon) unless otherwise noted. 1HN MR, 13CN MR, and 31PN MR
spectra were measured with aB ruker AVANCE 300 spectrometer or
aJ EOL JNM-ECZ400S (400 MHz) spectrometer.C hemical shifts of
1HN MR were expressed in parts per million downfield from CHCl3
as an internal standard (d = 7.26 ppm) in CDCl3,C 6H6 as an internal
standard (d = 7.16 ppm) in C6D6.C hemical shifts of 13CN MR were
expressed in parts per million downfield from CDCl3 as an internal
standard (d = 77.16 ppm) in CDCl3,C 6D6 as an internal standard
(d = 128.4 ppm). Chemical shifts of 31PN MR were expressed in
parts per million downfield from 85 %H 3PO4 as an external stan-
dard (d = 0p pm). Mass spectra were measured with aJ EOL JMS-
T100LC spectrometer.X -ray diffraction data were measured with a
Rigaku RAXIS-RAPID diffractometer.T he structures were solved by
ad irect method (SHELXL-2014).[23] The X-ray structure solution and
refinement were carried out by using the Yadokari-XG software.[24]
Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations were carried out by
using Gaussian 09 (B.01) package.[25]

Preparation of 3a
Am ixture of 1a (71.5 mg, 0.10 mmol) and (tht)AuCl (64.1 mg,
0.20 mmol) in dichloromethane (1 mL) was stirred for 1h at room
temperature. After the volatile materials were removed under re-
duced pressure, the resultant residue was dissolved in dichlorome-
thane (1 mL) under nitrogen atmosphere. The mixture was stirred
for 1h at room temperature, and the volatile materials were re-

Hydration of propargyla cetate[26]
To the corresponding chlorogold complex (3 mol %), as olution of
propargyl acetate (17.4 mg, 0.10 mmol) in acetone (1 mL) and H2O
(1.0 mmol) was added at room temperature. After stirring for 48 h,
the reaction mixture was directly loaded on as ilica gel (SiO2)
column and eluted with hexane/ethyl acetate 6:1t og ive 2-oxo-1-
phenylpropyl acetate as ac olorless oil.
Cycloisomerization of 1,6-enyne[27]
To the corresponding chlorogold complex (3 mol %), as olution of
1,6-enyne (25.3 mg, 0.10 mmol) in dichloromethane (1 mL) was
added at room temperature. After stirring for 24 h, the reaction
mixture was directly loaded on as ilica gel column and eluted with
hexane/ethyl acetate 6:1t og ive the cycloisomerization product as
ac olorless oil.
Alkoxycyclization of 1,6-enyne[27]
To the corresponding chlorogold complex (3 mol %), as olution of
1,6-enyne (25.3 mg, 0.10 mmol) in dichloromethane (0.5 mL) and
methanol (0.5 mL) was added at room temperature. After stirring
for 24 h, the reaction mixture was directly loaded on as ilica gel
column and eluted with hexane/ethyl acetate 6:1t og ive the prod-
uct as ac olorless oil.
Intramolecular hydroalkoxylation of allenyl alcohol[28]
Am ixture of 3b (5 mol %) and additive in toluene (0.4 mL) was
stirred for 10 min at room temperature. To the mixture in toluene
was added 2,2-diphenylhexa-4,5-dien-1-ol (25.3 mg, 0.10 mmol) in
toluene (0.6 mL) at room temperature. After stirring for 24 h, the
reaction mixture was directly loaded on as hort silica gel column
and eluted with hexane/ethyl acetate to give the 2-vinyltetrahydro-
furan as ac olorless oil.
